findings.title: Real marketplace installs never take the release-asset path: main is always -dev
findings.claim: The design keeps `main` at `X.Y.Z-dev` at all times except the few hours between a release commit and the next bump. A GitHub marketplace install reads the default branch, so every real user gets a `-dev` plugin. The resolver skips the download for `-dev`, so no real user ever fetches the published, checksummed engine. Every install needs Rust 1.97, a C compiler, the network and a build of 4 minutes or more. The documented upgrade also moves v0.1.0 users onto `-dev`. Nothing tests or spikes a GitHub-source install.
findings.evidence: architecture.md, Packaging and release, 'Versions and branches': "Between releases it carries `X.Y.Z-dev` ... An install from main between releases is a dev build: its version names no release, so its engine comes from source." Resolver step 4: "GitHub has no release asset for a `-dev` version, so without `PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL` the resolver skips this step." Owner checklist step 6 bumps `main` to `X.Y.(Z+1)-dev` right after tagging. 'Upgrade Planroom' tells users to run `/plugin marketplace update` and then `/plugin update`, which pulls main. DR-69 rejects a stable ref because "it needs a marketplace source that names a ref, which no spike has checked", so the gap is known and was left open. KICKOFF <constraints> Packaging says "the engine binary is fetched on first use from a GitHub release, checksum-verified ... The fallback is `cargo install --git` or a local build." Under this design the fallback is the only path for users. plugin-packaging.md §5 lists "Real git and GitHub marketplace installs" as not verified, and every S14 test uses a local-path marketplace. A second risk: a git marketplace keeps a full repo clone (Cargo.toml included) under `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/`. If Claude Code loads the plugin from that clone rather than the cache (unverified; the docs say the cache), the `<script dir>/../../Cargo.toml` checkout test matches. The rule that "in a checkout a build with another hash never falls through to the cache or a download" then blocks the download too.
findings.failure_scenario: v0.1.0 is published with four archives and SHA256SUMS. The next day a user runs `/plugin marketplace add doodla/planroom` and then `/plugin install planroom@planroom`. Main now says `0.1.1-dev`, so `engine.env` names no release. The resolver skips step 4 and runs the build preflight. Without cargo, the user gets one line telling them to install rustup, and with mods off the skill gets `engine_unavailable`. With cargo, the user waits for a 4-minute or longer build, and without Node and pnpm the build serves only the canvas fix page. Nobody downloads the published archives. A user who installed during the release window and later follows 'Upgrade Planroom' is moved to `-dev` and lands on the same path.
findings.proposed_fix: Make what users install name a release. In WS8, spike whether a marketplace plugin entry accepts a git ref (for example `{"source":"github","repo":"doodla/planroom","ref":"vX.Y.Z"}`), or whether `marketplace add` accepts a ref. If either works, have `gen --version` write the user-facing install to the tag, and keep `./plugin` for the local-path flow S14 and contributors use. If neither works, add a `release` branch that the owner fast-forwards to each tag (one more checklist click), and point the README's install line at it. Add an evidence step that installs from the public GitHub repo, with a branch or tag pushed by the owner, and shows `status --json` resolving at step 4. Make the checkout test positive (for example, `../../crates/planroom/Cargo.toml` exists and the path is not under the Claude Code plugins directory).

findings.title: The detached prefetch and build do not get their own process group on Linux
findings.claim: DR-69 says `prefetch --detach` and `build --detach` run "in its own process group (`set -m`)". On Ubuntu and Debian, `/bin/sh` is dash. dash turns job control off when no TTY is present, and the mod's `process.run` and the Bash tool have none. The background child therefore stays in the caller's process group, so any group-wide signal from Claude Code on reload, session end or a tool kill, or a terminal hangup, also kills the download or the build. The planned test checks only survival of parent exit, so it would pass while the guarantee fails.
findings.evidence: Verified in this container: `/bin/sh -> dash`. Running a script with `set -m; sleep 5 &` under `setsid dash` with stdin from /dev/null printed "set: can't access tty; job control turned off" and showed the child pgid equal to the parent's (21286/21286). bash under the same conditions gave the child its own pgid (21299). A-3 and A-10 (architecture.md, Assumptions) establish that the Bash tool and `process.run` run without a TTY. mod-api.md §7: "It is unverified whether the engine kills the child's process group or only its pid. A daemon that `setsid`s should survive either way." DR-69 dropped `setsid` for macOS's sake. The test is `tests/installer/run.sh::detach_returns_at_once_and_survives_parent_exit`, which covers parent exit only.
findings.failure_scenario: In the S14 evidence run on Linux, the mod deals "Build the engine from source, about 4 minutes?" and runs `scripts/planroom build --detach`. The cargo build runs in the resolver's process group. Then the plugin reloads (a `/reload-plugins`, or the edit-triggered reload of an in-place plugin) or the session ends. If Claude Code signals the group, the build dies part-way. The next start breaks the stale lock and deals the card again, so on a slow machine the engine never finishes building within one session. On a desktop, closing the terminal sends SIGHUP to the same group with the same result.
findings.proposed_fix: Detach in the resolver with `setsid` when it is on PATH (util-linux and BusyBox ship it on every Linux target). Fall back to `set -m` only under a shell that honours it without a TTY (macOS's `/bin/sh` is bash), and add `trap '' HUP` in both cases. Extend the installer test: on ubuntu-24.04 with `/bin/sh` as dash, assert that the child's session and pgid differ from the caller's, and that the child survives `kill -TERM -- -<caller pgid>` and SIGHUP. Keep the test on macos-15 as well.

findings.title: The engine-override guard blocks S14's own evidence step, while shared-cache poisoning stays possible
findings.claim: The engine-override variables are dangerous only because a download from any `PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL` lands in the shared cache `DATA_ROOT/engine/VERSION/` with a valid `.ok` stamp, which every later session then runs. The design guards this by denying agent Bash calls that set the variables. Any script or wrapper bypasses that rule, `cargo xtask` included. Meanwhile the build agent, whose own session loads the plugin from day one, is denied the plain command that S14's release-asset evidence needs.
findings.evidence: architecture.md, Actors (the guard): it denies "any call that sets ... `PLANROOM_ENGINE` or `PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL`, which pick the binary every later session runs". Packaging and release: step 3 reads the cache `DATA_ROOT/engine/VERSION/planroom` with a `.ok` stamp, and nothing restricts that cache to the default base. Step 4 accepts any https base, and SHA256SUMS comes from that same base. The S14 evidence path in feature_list.json requires "the release-asset path ... with PLANROOM_RESOLVE=release and PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL on a loopback server". KICKOFF <process> step 4 says "Load it all through the plugin install from day one", so the build session runs the mod's guard. The installer suite sets the variables inside scripts, which shows that the string-match guard does not see them.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) The build agent runs `PLANROOM_RESOLVE=release PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765 claude ...` to record the S14 tier A evidence. Its own mod denies the call, so the evidence needs a wrapper script, which means bypassing the project's own guardrail. (b) Scanned content injects a prompt into an agent. The agent uses Write to create `/tmp/x.sh` (allowed outside `.planroom/` and the data root), which removes `DATA_ROOT/engine/` and runs the resolver with `PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL=https://attacker.example`. The attacker's archive passes checks against the attacker's SHA256SUMS and is cached with a valid `.ok` stamp. Every later session's mod runs that binary and passes it each `PLANROOM_PERSON_TOKEN`, so the binary can turn its own ghosts into person-accepted edits.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the persistence instead of guarding the variable names. Cache a download from a non-default base only under a key derived from that base (for example `DATA_ROOT/engine-alt/<sha256(base)>/VERSION/`), and use it only when the same base is set again. Never cache a `PLANROOM_ENGINE` binary. Have `status --json` and `doctor` report a non-default source. The guard rule can then go, or stay as a warning. Name `cargo xtask live evidence S14` as the driver of the S14 evidence run: it sets the variables for the nested session and uses the `claude plugin marketplace add` and `claude plugin install` CLI forms that plugin-packaging §3 verified.

findings.title: The release dry run on workflow_dispatch fails the layout gate by design
findings.claim: `cargo xtask check` runs the layout gate's commit walk in CI, and the gate says a range it can't resolve "fails the check, never skips it". It defines ranges only for pushes and pull requests. The release workflow's `checks` job reruns `cargo xtask check`, and the owner's step 3 is a `workflow_dispatch` dry run, an event with no `before` and no pull request. So the dry run the checklist requires before tagging comes out red. ci.yml's own `workflow_dispatch` trigger hits the same failure.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md, Decision-record gate: "In CI, `check layout --commits RANGE` walks only the commits the push or pull request adds: `github.event.before..github.sha` for a push ..., the commits no other remote branch holds for a new branch or a force push, and the pull request's base to its head ... a range it can't resolve fails the check, never skips it." architecture.md, Release workflow: "2. `checks`: `cargo xtask check` and `cargo xtask test` again on the tagged commit". The trigger is "A tag push, or a `workflow_dispatch` on `main` that is a dry run by default". Owner checklist step 3: "Run Release by hand on `main`: a dry run". ci.yml (CI workflows) triggers on `workflow_dispatch` and allows only `cargo xtask` run steps (`ci_runs_only_xtask`), so no workflow can pass a range.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner merges the v0.1.0 release PR, sees CI green on main, and clicks Run workflow on Release. The `checks` job runs `cargo xtask check`, which finds a `workflow_dispatch` event with no `before`. The walk cannot resolve a range and fails. The dry run is red, so the owner stops before tagging, as the checklist intends, and v0.1.0 cannot be released by the documented procedure.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the walk per event. For `push` and `pull_request` (and a tag push's commits that no branch holds), walk as stated. For `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule` and the release workflow, run the state check only, since those commits were already walked when pushed to main. Add gate tests with the event payloads of a dispatch and a tag push.

findings.title: A -dev version names no build, so cached -dev engines go stale with a fix line that doesn't fix them
findings.claim: The cache is keyed by version alone, and the cache step checks only a sha256 stamp, never the catalogue hash that the checkout step checks. The source clone directory is also keyed by version. Every main commit between releases shares one `-dev` version string, so a cached `-dev` engine (built from a clone of main) keeps resolving after the plugin moves to a newer main. The mod's mismatch line then says to run `/reload-plugins`, which resolves the same stale binary. A plugin update at an unchanged version may also be ignored, because Claude Code keys its plugin cache by the `plugin.json` version (plugin-packaging §5).
findings.evidence: architecture.md, Packaging and release: step 2 compares `version --json` with the catalogue hash in `engine.env`, but step 3 is only "`DATA_ROOT/engine/VERSION/planroom`, with a `.ok` stamp holding its sha256". The clone build goes to `DATA_ROOT/src/VERSION`. Wiring step 2: "otherwise 'This Planroom engine doesn't match the plugin. Run /reload-plugins'". plugin-packaging.md §5: "The version resolves from `plugin.json` `version`, then the entry `version`, then the commit SHA" (from the guide, unverified). This compounds operability-1, under which every GitHub install is `-dev`.
findings.failure_scenario: A user on `0.1.1-dev` (catalogue H1) builds from a clone, and the binary is kept for `0.1.1-dev`. Later `/plugin marketplace update` and `/plugin update` bring a newer main (catalogue H2) with the same version. The resolver returns the cached H1 binary at step 3, and the mod shows the mismatch line. `/reload-plugins` changes nothing, and a rebuild finds `DATA_ROOT/src/0.1.1-dev` already present. If Claude Code ignores the update because the version didn't change, the user is stuck on the old main without knowing it.
findings.proposed_fix: Key the engine cache and the source clone by version plus catalogue hash (or the commit), and make step 3 check the catalogue hash as step 2 does. On a mismatch from a cached install, the line should offer the rebuild card rather than `/reload-plugins`. In WS8, check whether `/plugin update` picks up a new commit at an unchanged version. If it doesn't, have plain `gen` stamp `-dev` versions with a short catalogue hash.

findings.title: Older long-lived processes can write to a store that a newer engine has migrated
findings.claim: DR-1 says an older `watch` or `serve` "exits with `schema_mismatch` after a migration", but no mechanism is specified. Only `serve` is drained before a migration. The version check is described only at store open, and neither `store::commit` nor the `data_version` poll re-reads `PRAGMA user_version`. An older session's `watch` writes presence every 10 s and commits duty results, and it may do so against the migrated schema.
findings.evidence: decisions.md DR-1: "A newer binary asks an older `serve` to drain before migrating, and an older `watch` or `serve` exits with `schema_mismatch` after a migration". contracts.md, Store schema and migrations: "A binary that finds a newer `store_version` refuses ... One that finds an older one asks any older `serve` to drain ...", with no `watch` drain. architecture.md, The write path: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, idem lookup and insert, with no version re-check. Processes table: `watch` "writes presence every 10 s; runs duties under a lease".
findings.failure_scenario: Session A runs `/plugin update`, starts fresh, and its first command migrates the store to version N+1. Session B, still on the old plugin, keeps its `watch` running. Its next duty rescan commits facts and a `scan` event with version-N SQL into the N+1 tables. That either fails over and over as `duty_failed` or stores rows whose meaning the migration changed, and the new engine's fold then reads them.
findings.proposed_fix: Read `PRAGMA user_version` (and `meta.packs_hash`) inside every `store::commit` transaction and refuse with `schema_mismatch` when it differs from the version the process opened. Also re-read it whenever the `data_version` poll fires, so an older `watch` exits within 200 ms. Add a test in which a migration runs between an old writer's open and its commit.

findings.title: Machine-wide files have no cross-version compatibility or downgrade rule
findings.claim: The version-skew and downgrade design covers only the per-workspace `store.db`. Every engine version on the machine shares `DATA_ROOT/ledger.db` (which has its own migrations), `workspaces.json`, the event backups and the engine cache. A newer engine migrating the ledger therefore puts every older session in every workspace into `schema_mismatch`, not just the migrated workspace. A rollback to an older plugin has no way back for the ledger: `doctor --restore` and the `VACUUM INTO` copies cover only the store.
findings.evidence: contracts.md: "The ledger isn't in the store. It's `DATA_ROOT/ledger.db`, one per user, with its own migrations in `crates/store/ledger/`". Contracts versioning table: "the ledger's own `user_version`". The pre-migration copy and `doctor --restore BACKUP` (DR-53) name only `store-vN.db`. Persisted-document readers "refuse newer ones with `schema_mismatch`". The status line shows the ledger total on every `focus` (architecture.md, Status and toasts; DR-51).
findings.failure_scenario: A user with three Claude sessions in three workspaces updates the plugin in one of them. Its first billable call migrates `ledger.db`. The other two sessions, still on the old engine, now fail every `focus` that reads spend with `schema_mismatch`, although their stores were never touched. If the new release turns out bad and the user reinstalls the previous version, that version refuses the ledger with no restore path, so the user must delete it and lose the daily spend guard's history.
findings.proposed_fix: For the ledger and the other data-root files, allow only additive migrations and record a `min_reader_version`, so older engines keep reading a newer ledger. Take a `VACUUM INTO` copy before each ledger migration and let `doctor --restore` cover it. Document the data root's compatibility rule in Contracts next to the store's.

findings.title: No supported engine install behind a blocking proxy, and the env passthrough fallback is incomplete
findings.claim: When a corporate proxy blocks GitHub's release CDN or the crates index, the resolver offers only the source build (whose preflight then fails) or `PLANROOM_ENGINE`. That variable is unverified, does not persist, and agents may not set it. No command takes an archive downloaded by hand and verifies and caches it. Separately, A-14's fallback forwards only `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and `SSL_CERT_FILE`, but this very container depends on `https_proxy`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` and `CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO` as well.
findings.evidence: architecture.md, Packaging and release: on a failed download a non-mod caller gets `engine_unavailable` naming `scripts/planroom build`. The source build preflight checks "a reachable crates index". Neither error names the archive URL or a manual install. A-14's fallback: "the mod passes `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` to the resolver by name". Verified in this container: `https_proxy`, `no_proxy`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` are set. iris-release-bar.md §3 and DR-28 record a 403 from this proxy on `releases/latest`, so partial GitHub blocking is a real pattern here.
findings.failure_scenario: A user behind a TLS-inspecting proxy can reach github.com but not the asset CDN, and cannot reach crates.io. The prefetch fails, the build preflight says the crates index is unreachable, and Planroom does nothing at all, with no instruction for the obvious fix of downloading the archive in a browser. In the A-14 fallback case, curl and cargo lose the CA bundle and the lowercase proxy variables, so the download and the build fail TLS even on a network that works.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `scripts/planroom install-archive PATH [SHA256SUMS]`. It verifies the archive against SHA256SUMS, or against a hash printed in the error line, checks the layout, and caches it as a download would. Make the failed-download line name the exact archive and SHA256SUMS URLs and this command. In the A-14 fallback, forward both cases of the proxy variables and the CA variables (`CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO`, `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`), or the whole session environment.

verdicts.reason: Nothing in the design handles this. It says outright that an install from main between releases builds from source, and main carries -dev at every point except the short window between the release commit and the next bump. A GitHub marketplace add reads the default branch, so the published, checksummed archives are never used by a real install. That goes against KICKOFF's packaging constraint that the engine is fetched on first use from a GitHub release, with a local build only as the fallback. DR-69 saw the gap and rejected a stable ref only because no spike had checked it. That leaves the gap open; it does not handle it. S14's own tier A steps use a local-path marketplace and would still pass, but the constraint violation alone makes this material.

Step 4: "GitHub has no release asset for a `-dev` version, so without `PLANROOM_RELEASE_BASE_URL` the resolver skips this step". Owner checklist step 6 bumps main to X.Y.(Z+1)-dev. DR-69, Alternatives rejected: "A `stable` branch for installs: it needs a marketplace source that names a ref, which no spike has checked". KICKOFF <constraints> Packaging: "the engine binary is fetched on first use from a GitHub release ... The fallback is `cargo install --git` or a local build." plugin-packaging.md §5: "Real git and GitHub marketplace installs" not verified. feature_list S14 install steps use LOCAL_REPO_PATH / $REPO only.

The design's only isolation mechanism for prefetch and build is `set -m` (DR-69 dropped setsid), and its claim that a reload doesn't kill the child depends on that isolation. mod-api §7 says it is unverified whether the host kills a whole process group. If it does, a Linux S14 evidence run that reloads during the 4-minute detached build loses the build. The planned test checks only survival of parent exit, so it would not catch this. verdicts.reason: Part (a) is mostly handled already. Evidence runs go through the one task entry point, `cargo xtask live evidence SNN`, which sets variables for nested sessions itself. The agent's Bash call then names no PLANROOM_* variable, so the guard does not fire, and no hand-made wrapper is needed. Part (b) is real, since a download from a non-default base is stored in the shared cache. It adds no capability, though. The design says the guard is a guardrail and not a security boundary between processes of one OS user. The guard also does not stop Bash from writing into DATA_ROOT/engine/ directly: its Bash deny list covers only the stores, ledger, backups and login pages. So a prompt-injected agent can already replace the cached binary without these variables. Keying alternate-base downloads separately would be cleaner, but it is not a material defect.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md, Testing strategy table: "Evidence runs | `cargo xtask live evidence SNN` | live Jev, gateway and plugin session". architecture.md, line 973: "`cargo xtask live` passes the variable into nested sessions". Actors also says: "This is a guardrail for 'AI proposes, person disposes', not a security boundary between processes of one OS user, and `SECURITY.md` says so."
